evidence: Cic. Att. 12.37.1: plānē bellē sē habēre
Traupman 107: I simply don’t know what he is thinking of, jam plānē quid cōgitet nesciō
terms.comment: Nōn plānē is “not quite”. Traupman gives admodum for “quite” and parum, “too little”, for “not quite” (p. 367).

terms.gloss: absolutely, utterly; with a negative, at all
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.14: ita prōrsus exīstimō (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Heaut. 776: nam prōrsum nihil intelligō

terms.gloss: altogether, entirely; with a negative, at all
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.42: tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint

terms.gloss: quite, very; with numbers, fully, just about
evidence: Liv. 21.36.2: in pedum mīlle admodum altitūdinem

phrases.latin: quod reliquōs cohērēdēs convēnistī, plānē bene
phrases.english: as for your meeting the other co-heirs, quite right

phrases.latin: age, sī quō abīre est animus, est licentia? — nōn plānē est, inquit.
phrases.english: “Come now, if you want to go off somewhere, are you allowed?” “Not quite,” he said.

phrases.latin: in here neque E plānē neque I audītur
phrases.english: in here you hear neither quite an e nor quite an i
